summary: Kathleen Kenyon was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at St Paul's Girls' School (~1918–1925) and Somerville College (~1925–1928). She held posts at the University of London and UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She held appointments at DePauw University (~1986–1987), the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1987–1988), Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe (~1974–1984), Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974–2023), and the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche (all attested 2010).
Kathrin Holz specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown studied at Juniata College, the University of Michigan under Walter M. Spink, and the University of Utah Hospital. Active in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, she is a Complex Family Planning Fellow at the University of Utah (2024–2026).
Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Her career includes posts attested at Victoria University of Wellington in 1998 and the University of Manitoba in 1999.

Katia Buffetrille is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD at Paris Nanterre University (~1986–1996) under Alexander W. Macdonald. She has been affiliated with CRCAO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Études mongoles, sibériennes, centrasiatiques et tibétaines.

Katia Chirkova is a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist. She studied at Beijing Language and Culture University (1995–1998) and Leiden University (PhD 2003), later holding posts at Leiden University (2003–2005), IIAS (2005–2006), and CRLAO (2006).

Katja Triplett is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Marburg (1996–2002). Her career includes posts at Marburg, SOAS, the University of Munich, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Leipzig.

Katragadda Paddayya is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral degree at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1968) and served as a professor, including Professor of Geo-archaeology, at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1970–2008).

Katrin Querl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Munich, Kagyu College, and the University of Vienna, and has held academic posts at the University of Leipzig and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He held teaching posts at Kokugakuin University and the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1965–1969) and served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1996–2016).

Katsuji Fujioka was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933, succeeding Kazutoshi Ueda.
Katsumi Kuroita was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held a post there from approximately 1902 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held multiple academic posts at Kyoto University from 1975 to 2010.

Katsumi Okimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1973). He spent his academic career at Hanazono University, serving as professor (~1985–2009), director, and professor emeritus (~2009–2014).

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1968) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–1998) and Chuo University (~1998–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, historian, and scholar of Sinology and Buddhism who studied at Kyoto University. He held positions at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University, Kansai University, Nara National Museum, and Ryukoku University.

Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MSU Baroda, and Panjab University. She held positions at the College of Art, Delhi, Marg Publications, and served as dean at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2001.
